![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14228914/assets/9ceef67f02c022065be31de7ec1b6785d270c194aee29c4d0a20707998932134.png)

Given the triangle above, find the length of $\overset{―}{BC}$ rounded to one decimal place.
question.worked_solution:
For an angle $\theta $ in a right triangle, the trigonometric ratios are as follows:

- $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =\frac{\text{opposite leg}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$

- $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =\frac{\text{adjacent leg}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$

- $\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{\text{opposite leg}}{\text{adjacent leg}}$

First, note that we are given the length of the hypotenuse $\overset{―}{AB}$ and wish to find the length of the leg $\overset{―}{BC}$ adjacent to the given angle $∠B.$

The trigonometric ratio that relates the adjacent leg to the hypotenuse is *cosine*. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(m∠B) & =\frac{\text{adjacent leg}}{\text{hypotenuse}} \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡({38}^{∘}) & =\frac{BC}{12} \\ BC & =12\operatorname{cos}⁡({38}^{∘}).\end{aligned}
$$

Using a calculator to evaluate the trigonometric ratio, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & =12\operatorname{cos}⁡({38}^{∘}) \\  & =12(0.788\,01…) \\  & =9.456\,12… \\  & ≈9.5,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to one decimal place.
